strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN for OpenWrt/Linux to Linux or Windows using unordered FakeTCP/FEC carriers plus a native standards-compliant DTLS 1.3 WBD security/session layer. Xray/VLESS/Vision/REALITY, WireGuard and Android are not part of the V2.1 product stack.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: V2-M3 native WBD session/control inside the locally qualified one-lane DTLS/FEC/FakeTCP path
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: M2 is complete. During M3, add only product/session semantics inside an already-finished DTLS 1.3 association. Do not invent another cryptographic layer, reliable public byte stream or custom FEC. Do not start two-lane, kernel-anchor, TUN/L3, Windows, Auto or detector-specific shaping work before the M3 session/control gate passes.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Completed full V2-M2 qualification. Substantive product/evidence commit 2a1cbd8a5c0cb040b293b7f03b44d18dcb927014 updates the DTLS shim to quiet-by-default tracing, adds the reproducible M2C harness, raw CSV/median data, report/receipt and marks deps/security-lock.json fully qualified. The exact pinned one-lane topology UDPspeeder mode0 FEC -> wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 -> udp2raw FakeTCP was run locally at approximately 50 ms RTT with 200 x 256 B payloads, window32 and 64-packet warmup. Primary 20:20 covered 0/1/5/10/15% encrypted-record loss across seeds 260824/260825/260826: all 15 cases delivered 200/200, with median p99 about 70.5/71.9/76.2/69.8/82.1 ms and median security byte overhead about 5.2-5.4% relative to the matching M1 UDPspeeder FEC bytes. Secondary 20:10 regression at 0/1/15% covered 9 cases, all 200/200, with median p99 about 72.3/71.9/79.0 ms. Formal single-run outliers were preserved; deterministic repeats reduced the worst tails, supporting sandbox scheduling sensitivity rather than ordered-record HOL. Quiet-default M2B was requalified after tracing changes: one encrypted record was dropped and later msg-02/msg-03 still decrypted and delivered. Continuity test commit da50221c33f920c374c9a6fb695cb458de8ea643 advances the persisted invariants from architecture-pinned to full-M2-qualified state. GitHub handoff-verify, Go tests and handoff tests pass on that tree.
continuation_cursor.current_task: V2-M3A: define and implement the smallest versioned native WBD control framing that runs only after DTLS Finished. Start with HELLO, ACCEPT and ERROR control messages plus strict header/length/version validation; keep the codec carrier-agnostic and do not add credentials, keepalive, reconnect policy or TUN yet.
continuation_cursor.why_now: The weak-network carrier and the standards-based security layer are now independently and jointly qualified. The next missing product layer is explicit WBD session semantics. Starting with a tiny version-negotiation/control codec keeps failures diagnosable and avoids mixing authentication, routing or reconnect behavior into the first protocol commitment.
continuation_cursor.done_when: M3A has a documented minimal control-frame format with a fixed magic/version/type/length boundary, deterministic encode/decode behavior, HELLO->ACCEPT success negotiation, unsupported-version->ERROR behavior, strict rejection of truncated/oversized/unknown-invalid frames, and unit/fuzz-style malformed coverage. A loopback integration must prove these control frames are exchanged only as DTLS application data after Finished. No custom crypto or lower-carrier changes are part of M3A.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: V2-M3A: inspect existing carrier-agnostic framing code for safe reuse, then add a minimal WBD control codec for HELLO/ACCEPT/ERROR with an explicit protocol version and bounded payload length. Write table-driven encode/decode and malformed/version tests first. After the codec tests pass, run the smallest direct-DTLS loopback negotiation using the already-qualified wbd.test certificate path. Do not add username/password/token auth until this framing gate passes.

security.placement: UDPspeeder source/repair datagram -> DTLS application datagram -> udp2raw FakeTCP
